Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise plan we can action in the kickoff. I attached a sample promptset template and a short integration doc (redwood-promptset-v1.csv, eval-harness-integration.md).

High-level onboarding steps
1) Promptset ingest: you can upload CSV (columns: id,prompt,expected_label,accept_fail,notes). We’ll map to our eval harness and run an initial baseline against the model variant you plan to serve.
2) Baseline & thresholds: we’ll compute a pass-rate (fraction of prompts labeled accept). For AcmePay I propose initial thresholds:
   - Minimum pass-rate: 92% baseline over the full promptset
   - Canary pass-rate tolerance: no >4 percentage-point drop vs. baseline over 60m window
   - Latency: P95 < 800ms for 95% of canary requests
3) Canary rollout: start with 3% traffic for 48 hours, then 10% for 24 hours if metrics stable.
4) Automated rollback policy: trigger rollback if any of the following during canary window:
   - Pass-rate drop > 6 percentage points sustained for 30 minutes
   - P95 latency increase > 300ms over baseline for 15 minutes
   - Error rate (5xx + model errors) > 0.5% sustained 10 minutes
5) Alerts & paging: minor alerts (pass-rate drop 2–4 pp) -> slack + email to CS/Eng; major alerts (>=6 pp or high error rate) -> page oncall and auto-failover to fallback model.
6) Eval harness integration: we’ll run nightly regression checks, and connect your testset to our webhook so you get early-run alerts.

Action items for kickoff
- Olivia: upload CSV using the template and confirm which model variant we should baseline against.
- Monica/Marissa: confirm alert routing and escalation matrix.
- Diego: prepare the canary routing rule and fallback model mapping; note any export constraints for logs.

I put the runbook link in the related_links field. Happy to adjust thresholds in the kickoff with you all.

— Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple operational details we should capture during the kickoff:

- Eval harness outputs: we’ll provide per-prompt verdicts, confidence scores, and a semantic-quality score (0–1) that aggregates across clusters. Please ensure your accept_fail labels are consistent across annotators; otherwise we’ll run a small relabeling pass.
- Regression alerts: default regression detector looks for 3-sigma drops over the trailing 7-day window, but for outbound-facing payments flows we should use a conservative detection: absolute drop thresholds (pp) as Soojin suggested + rolling window persistence.
- Canary slicing: we recommend slicing canary traffic by user segment (10% of internal staff + 3% of real traffic) so you can validate behavior on known accounts before broader exposure.
- Telemetry exports: we need request_id, prompt_id, model_variant, latency_ms, pass_fail, semantic_score, and a hashed user_id to meet privacy constraints. If you cannot provide hashed user_id, we can use session buckets.

If it helps, I’ll bring the eval templates and a proposed tagging scheme to the kickoff.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Quick technical clarifications from infra side so the integration is smooth:

- CSV size: 150 prompts is fine. If you plan to expand later, the harness supports up to 20k rows; we recommend sharding large sets into labeled cohorts.
- Webhook replay: our eval harness can POST per-run summaries to your endpoint. We need a URL and an HMAC key for auth.
- KV caching & canary latency: if your app pins prompts or uses long-context sessions, call this out — caching will change latency baselines. We should capture a small set of cached vs uncached prompts in the baseline.
- Rollback automation: we’ll provide a job that flips routing to fallback model and records a signed rollback event. We’ll want a manual confirmation boolean before an irreversible rollback in prod — automation will be opt-in for the kickoff window.

Two asks for AcmePay before kickoff: 1) an endpoint for webhook test (staging is fine), 2) confirm whether session-level caching is used.

— Diego
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
